title: Active learning identifies salt-rich media for flaviolin production
summary: An automated recommendation tool proposed culture-medium mixtures for engineered Pseudomonas putida across three semi-automated campaigns. The paper reports direct flaviolin-titer improvements of about 70% and 60% in two campaigns and a 350% process-yield improvement in a third, each versus its campaign starting medium. The spectroscopic proxy changed by different amounts, so proxy values are not substituted for direct quantification. Results are specific to the tested strain, media and objective and do not establish industrial performance. A preprint preceded the journal article, but its exact posting date and version-specific outcome set are unresolved; the journal date is used without asserting first disclosure.
ai_technology: Automated Recommendation Tool for active-learning medium optimization
organization: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; Department of Energy Agile BioFoundry; Joint BioEnergy Institute; Sandia National Laboratories; University of California, Berkeley; BCAM, Basque Center for Applied Mathematics

source_review.scope: Primary publisher article/PDF and institutional preprint metadata reviewed for identity, bounded outcomes, AI role, affiliations and chronology.

evidence.tested: Primary article reports direct titer changes of about 70% and 60% in two campaigns and a 350% yield change in a third, with each comparison tied to its own starting medium.
evidence.unknown: Outcomes are specific to the engineered strain and the tested campaigns; the earlier preprint date/version contents and independent replication are not established.
evidence.ai_role: The Automated Recommendation Tool proposed media formulations iteratively from experimental measurements; feature-importance analysis highlighted salt effects, but does not prove a unique causal mechanism.
